answer: Interleaved arrival gating. Each identity must submit its first three actions across separate, randomly assigned time windows; a glacier pacing curve enforces slow early throughput, and a trellis of cross-checks links latecomers to earlier window timestamps. An attacker minting many identities pays a fixed delay cost per identity, roughly the window length times queue position, before any action clears. The crystal test is timestamp entropy: bulk registrations cluster in narrow bands and are rejected.
